and `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/deploy-port.ts:29` records the same measurement: "excluding tests returns zero. So a `deployment.set_target` dispatch has no affordance to [spend]".
So the browser is not missing a button by oversight - it is correctly refusing to render a control that would have no affordance to spend. THE PRODUCER IS THE MISSING PIECE, and this row is it.

THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE AS task-2cedb26a598540bd9bab17046592a7bb (the `deployment.deploy` per-goal offer, planned 2026-09-06). THE GRANULARITY DIFFERS FROM THE DEPLOY OFFER, AND THAT IS THE DECISION THIS ROW MUST MAKE. `deployment.set_target`'s payload keys are `["environment", "network", "sshTarget", "url"]` (daemon-command-payload-keys.ts:165) and the durable target is keyed `deploy-target:<projectId>:<environment>` (deploy-target-contracts.ts:84) - so unlike `deployment.deploy`, whose environment is chosen at dispatch from a single goal-scoped offer, BINDING is a per-(project, environment) act. Decide whether the offer is goal-scoped with the environment in the payload, or one per environment, and state it in a comment at the offer site the way task-2cedb26a requires. Do not leave the browser to infer it.

WITHHOLDING IS THE INVERSE OF THE DEPLOY OFFER'S. A deploy offer is withheld when NO target is bound; a set_target offer is what an operator needs precisely THEN. Say what the rule is - it is not "withheld when already bound", because rebinding is legitimate.
